npc_studio.server.no_session.title: The server is checking accounts
npc_studio.server.no_session.body: This game is not signed in to an account Mojang will confirm, and the server asks them about everyone who joins — it will refuse whatever password is given. Either run the game signed in, or turn the check off. On a server at 127.0.0.1 that nobody else can reach, turning it off costs nothing real; on one open to the world it means anybody can join under any name. Operator rights given earlier are rewritten to the new identifiers of the same names — otherwise they would simply stop working.

npc_studio.server.eula.title: The Minecraft agreement
npc_studio.server.eula.body: A Minecraft server may only be run by someone who has accepted Mojang's agreement. Pressing accept records that you agree to it — nobody can do that on your behalf. The file is written into this server's folder and no other.

npc_studio.server.key.title: %s — access key
npc_studio.server.key.terms: You paste the key yourself and it stays yours. This mod keeps it on your own disk and cannot answer for it being lost, leaked or revoked — the file is on your computer, and what other programs and other people do with it is out of anyone's reach here. The terms for using their API are between you and them; this mod is not a party to those and is not connected with them. If something goes wrong, write and we will try to help.
npc_studio.server.browse.failed: The catalogue refused — the reason is on the right
npc_studio.server.key.how: %s will not answer without an access key belonging to whoever is using it. One key shipped inside a mod would be one account's quota and one account's name on every request in the world, and they revoke those — so this asks for yours. Make one on their site, it is free, and paste it below.
npc_studio.server.key.where: Where it goes: a file beside the game's settings, written so that only your account may read it, and never anywhere near a server folder. It is sent in a header to that one site and to nothing else, on a request that will not follow a redirect anywhere. It is never written to a log and never shown again in full. What cannot be promised: it is not encrypted, because this mod has to be able to read it to use it — anything running as you can read it too, exactly as with a key saved in your browser.

npc_studio.server.worlds.no_copies: No copies yet. A copy is taken with the button on a world, and by itself before anything that cannot be undone.
npc_studio.server.worlds.name: Name
npc_studio.server.worlds.make_says: The core makes the world: the server starts once, generates it and stops itself. This window closes at once — the strip along the top shows how far along it is, and you can get on with something else. An own type only works if the mod that adds it is installed on the server.
npc_studio.server.worlds.use_body: This writes one line — level-name — and the server reads it the next time it starts. It will then play %s.
npc_studio.server.worlds.use_body_runnin: This writes one line — level-name — and the server reads it only when it starts. The one that is running now keeps playing what it loaded until it is stopped and started again. It will then play %s.
npc_studio.server.worlds.used_restart: %s will be played on the next start
npc_studio.server.worlds.saving_first: Copying what is there now first…
npc_studio.server.worlds.failed: That did not work — the reason is below
npc_studio.server.worlds.restore_body: Everything in %s is replaced by what it was on %s. A copy of what is there now is taken first, so today is not lost by going back to last week.
npc_studio.server.worlds.save_off.title: The server is not saving
npc_studio.server.worlds.save_off.body: It was told to stop writing for a copy, and the command to let it write again did not get through. Until it does, everything since then is only in memory and a crash loses it. Send save-on in the console, or restart the server.
npc_studio.server.worlds.replace_pick: A dimension folder — the one with region in it
npc_studio.server.worlds.replace_running: Stop the server first. Swapping files under a loaded dimension hands it chunks that no longer exist, and it will write its own back over the ones you brought.
npc_studio.server.worlds.replace_body: The chunks of %s in %s will be replaced by whatever is in the folder %s. The rest — the seed, the spawn, the players, the maps — stays: it is the same world with a different dimension. The old chunks do not go to a bin, they are gone, so a copy of the whole world is taken first.
npc_studio.server.worlds.make_wait: The core is running. It is what makes the world — with its mods, its dimensions and its generator. You need not keep this window open; the work is not happening in it.
npc_studio.server.worlds.make_running: Stop the server first: making a world is a start of the core, and the core is busy with the world it has loaded.
npc_studio.server.worlds.bad_name: A folder cannot be called that: letters, digits, dash, underscore and dot.
npc_studio.server.worlds.taken: There is already a folder called %s
npc_studio.server.worlds.step_making: The core is generating the world…
npc_studio.server.worlds.step_stopping: The world is there; stopping the core…
npc_studio.server.worlds.core_left: The core left without making the world. The reason is in the last lines of the console: usually an unaccepted EULA, or a world type the server does not know.
npc_studio.server.worlds.too_long: The core did not answer in fifteen minutes. It is still running — look at the console.
npc_studio.server.worlds.slow_stop: The core did not stop within three minutes. The world may well be made, but the folder is still being written — wait for it to stop and read the list again.
npc_studio.server.worlds.no_level_dat: The core ran and there is no world folder. Look at the console: most likely it would not take the type or the seed.
npc_studio.server.worlds.reset_body: The chunks of %s in %s will be deleted, and the server will generate it again the next time somebody walks in — same seed, same generator, a fresh dimension. Everything built there goes; the seed, the spawn, the players and the other dimensions stay. A copy of the whole world is taken first.
npc_studio.server.worlds.make_says_flat: Layers are written bottom upwards. The core makes the world: the server starts once, generates it and stops itself — this window closes at once and the strip along the top shows how far along it is.
npc_studio.server.worlds.make_says_debug: A debug world is a grid of every block in every state it has. Nothing can be built or broken in it; it is there to be looked at. The core makes it like any other.
npc_studio.server.worlds.drop_body: %s (%s) goes entirely — every dimension, every player, every map. A copy is taken first and stays in the copies tab: it is the only thing that can bring it back.
npc_studio.server.worlds.drop_body_curre: This is the world the server is set to play. It goes entirely, and on its next start the server will make an empty world of the same name — which looks exactly like this one having been emptied. A copy is taken first and stays in the copies tab.
npc_studio.server.worlds.dropping: A copy first, then the deleting…
npc_studio.server.worlds.dropped: %s is gone; the copy is not
npc_studio.server.worlds.drop_running: Stop the server first: it holds the world's files open and is writing to them.
npc_studio.server.places.says: A dimension is added by a datapack in the world folder — no plugins, no mods. It appears on the server's next start: dimensions are read when the world loads, and /reload does not add them.
npc_studio.server.places.none: None yet. The usual one is a flat or empty place for builders, which they go to by a command and come back from.
npc_studio.server.places.name: Name
npc_studio.server.places.point_hint: x y z in the main world
npc_studio.server.places.window_says: Nobody is given permissions: the list becomes scores on the server, and people travel by /trigger — the one command an ordinary player may use. The order of the names decides the plots, so changing it moves people.
npc_studio.server.places.drop_body: %s (%s) goes out of the datapack. The folder holding its chunks stays in the world — we do not touch it, because somebody's work is in there. Making it again with the same id brings it back.
npc_studio.server.places.restart_body: The datapack is written. Dimensions are read when the world loads, so a new one appears on the server's next start — /reload will not add it. The list of who may go, and the commands themselves, are re-read by /reload as well.
npc_studio.server.packs.title: Datapacks
npc_studio.server.packs.stop_first: Stop the server first: it holds the world's files open.
npc_studio.server.packs.says: Which packs are on is not kept in the folder but in the world itself, in level.dat. The server is down, so that is written directly and takes effect on its next start.
npc_studio.server.packs.says_running: The server is up, so the switch goes as a command and takes effect at once. Dimensions still only appear when the world loads: a pack that adds one cannot be switched on mid-flight.
npc_studio.server.packs.drop_body: %s goes out of %s for good. Everything it added — dimensions, recipes, functions — goes with it; anything built in its dimension stays in the world folder but becomes unreachable.
npc_studio.server.places.reloaded: The server has re-read its datapacks
npc_studio.server.browse.into_plugins_br: The plugins folder (needs the bridge mod)
npc_studio.server.places.remake_body: The type is changed and written, but the ground already generated stays as it was — while its chunks are there the server shows the old one. Delete them and let the server make the dimension again from the new type? Anything built there goes; a copy of the whole world is taken first.
npc_studio.server.places.remade: Done — it will be made again when somebody walks in

npc_studio.server.configs.unreadable: This does not read as settings; most likely the format is broken somewhere. Open it with "Edit the file" and look.
npc_studio.server.configs.running: The server is running: this file is read at start, so the change arrives after a restart.

npc_studio.server.configs.not_yet: No settings yet — they appear after the server has run once

npc_studio.server.players.op_body: %s will get every server command, including stopping it, giving items and making others operators. It can be taken back with the same button.
npc_studio.server.players.deop_body: %s stays on the server but can no longer run operator commands.
npc_studio.server.players.ban_body: %s will not be able to join, and will be thrown off if they are on now. The same button undoes it.
npc_studio.server.players.pardon_body: %s will be able to join again.
npc_studio.server.players.kick_body: %s will drop off the server, and can join again straight away.
npc_studio.server.players.kick_stopped: Kicking needs a running server — there is nobody on a stopped one.
npc_studio.server.players.list.empty: The lists are empty — whatever you decide about people and addresses appears here.
npc_studio.server.players.list.bad_name: A name is letters, digits and underscores, up to 16 characters.
npc_studio.server.players.list.bad_ip: That does not look like an address.
npc_studio.server.players.list.enforce_h: While the whitelist is not enforced anybody can join, however many names are on it. This is the same white-list line of server.properties that the Settings tab shows.
npc_studio.server.players.ban_ip_body: Nobody will get in from %s — and behind one address there may be a household, a school or a mobile network. The same button undoes it.
npc_studio.server.players.ban_address_bo: %s will be banned along with the address they are playing from. A household, a school, a hall of residence or a mobile network all share one address, so this reaches people who have done nothing. It can be lifted on the Lists half.
npc_studio.server.players.ban_address_hi: Ban the address this player is connected from right now.
npc_studio.server.players.ban_address_of: The server knows the address only while the player is online — it writes it down nowhere. Once they have left, the address can be typed in by hand on the Lists half.

npc_studio.server.rights.pick: Choose a privilege on the left to look at it and change it.
npc_studio.server.rights.nothing_to_inhe: Nothing to inherit: there are no other privileges.
npc_studio.server.rights.can_none: None of its own — only what it inherits.
npc_studio.server.rights.create_body: Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore — the name goes into a command, and a space in it makes that a different command. It can be shown under any name at all; that is what the other field is for.
npc_studio.server.rights.create_hint: Create a new privilege in LuckPerms
npc_studio.server.rights.drop_body: “%s” goes, along with all its permissions, and everybody who had it loses it. This cannot be undone.
npc_studio.server.rights.bad_group: A name is letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, up to 36 characters.
npc_studio.server.rights.group_there: There is already a privilege called “%s”.
npc_studio.server.rights.bad_node: A node cannot be empty and cannot contain spaces.
npc_studio.server.rights.bad_weight: A weight is a whole number.
npc_studio.server.rights.stopped: Rights change only on a running server: a plugin keeps them, not a file.
npc_studio.server.rights.no_export: LuckPerms did not produce the export. It answers nothing over the command channel, so the reason is only visible in the server console.
npc_studio.server.rights.no_plugin: This server has no named privileges: without a permission plugin there are four operator levels and nothing else, and any name this window invented would be a name no server obeys. What each level does is read off the game's own command tree — an explanation, not data out of a file.
npc_studio.server.players.op_level_body: %s will be given operator rights: %s. Only somebody with at least as much can take that back.
